title: Google TPU 8tx Pairs AMD EPYC Turin Hosts with Confidential Computing while TPU 8i Max Doubles Memory Bandwidth
gist: Google added two eighth-gen TPU systems: TPU 8tx (TPU 8t silicon paired with dual-socket AMD EPYC Turin hosts for confidential computing, on the low-latency Boardfly network) and TPU 8i Max (two TPU 8i chips in one package, 384 GB HBM at 17.2 TB/s, 768 MB SRAM) aimed at memory-bound long-context agentic inference. STH frames the 8tx host socket as a meaningful hyperscaler design win for AMD EPYC and its confidential computing features rather than a share-moving event.

insights.claim: Google now offers four distinct eighth-generation TPU system configurations in a single year (8t, 8i, 8tx, 8i Max), the first time it has done so, but these are not four new chip designs — 8tx reuses TPU 8t silicon and 8i Max packages two 8i chips.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Google is extracting more SKUs from fewer tape-outs, segmenting by workload and customer — watch for similar product-proliferation from other custom-ASIC hyperscalers.
insights.quote: This marks the first time Google has introduced four distinct system configurations in a single year, though it is not four new chip designs.
insights.locator: Google is expanding its eighth-generation TPU portfolio

insights.claim: Google's inference-focused TPU 8i uses a Boardfly network topology with a maximum hop diameter of seven versus sixteen hops in the training-oriented torus, reducing latency for real-time reasoning.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Interconnect topology is becoming workload-specific; inference fabrics optimized for hop count differ from training torus designs.

insights.claim: STH's read is that Google is tailoring TPU offerings not just to different parts of the AI stack but to different customers, with 8tx a customized confidential-computing product and 8i Max designed for inference.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Custom silicon lets hyperscalers build customer-segment-specific SKUs (e.g. regulated/government), widening the competitive moat vs merchant GPUs in those niches.
insights.quote: Google is tailoring its TPU offerings for different parts of the AI stack, and really even different customers.

insights.claim: Google's TPU 8tx targets regulated enterprises and governments running frontier or proprietary models on sensitive data, using confidential computing to encrypt data in use inside an isolated trusted execution environment.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Confidential AI compute opens regulated/sovereign workloads to cloud TPUs — a demand vector for Google Cloud in government and finance.
insights.locator: The TPU 8tx is the third system

insights.claim: TPU 8tx pairs TPU 8t silicon with custom 5th Gen AMD EPYC 'Turin' hosts; a dual-socket Turin configuration provides 128 PCIe Gen5 lanes, giving zero I/O oversubscription across four TPUs plus high-speed NICs.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Host-CPU lane count is a selection criterion in accelerator trays; AMD's I/O-rich EPYC wins sockets on that basis.

insights.claim: Google said a PCIe Gen6 host such as AMD EPYC Venice would step down to Gen5 speeds with the TPU 8t without adding accelerator bandwidth, so Turin fits its 2027 hardware qualification schedule.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Accelerator I/O generation, not CPU newness, dictates host choice — prior-gen CPUs can keep winning AI host sockets, extending product lifecycles.
insights.locator: Google noted that a Gen6 host

insights.claim: TPU 8tx adopts the inference-oriented Boardfly network rather than the training torus, and Google claims up to 2x lower latency than TPU 8t with a near-zero performance penalty, benefiting multi-step agents that make many sequential inference calls.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Agentic workloads reward low per-call latency; topology choices are a lever hyperscalers use to differentiate inference products.
insights.locator: The 8tx also adopts the Boardfly network

insights.claim: Google told STH that customers whose data must remain within the confidential computing domain should use TPU 8tx for inference and serving, not the 8i Max.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Confidential workloads are fenced onto a specific SKU, implying 8i Max lacks the TEE host pairing.
insights.locator: We asked and Google told us

insights.claim: TPU 8i Max combines two TPU 8i chips in one multi-chip package, doubling compute, SRAM (to 768 MB) and HBM bandwidth (to 17.2 TB/s) versus a single TPU 8i, with 384 GB of HBM — about a third more capacity than TPU 8i.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: HBM bandwidth per package doubles while capacity grows only ~33% — more HBM stacks/bandwidth content per accelerator supports HBM supplier demand.
insights.locator: Google TPU 8i Max Packs Two Chips

insights.claim: When many agents work across an entire codebase or hours of video simultaneously, memory bandwidth becomes the bottleneck before compute does, which is the design rationale for TPU 8i Max.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Long-context agentic inference is memory-bandwidth bound — favors HBM and SRAM-heavy designs over raw FLOPS.
insights.quote: memory bandwidth becomes the bottleneck before compute does

insights.claim: STH argues the TPU 8tx host socket will not drive a 10% server CPU market share gain for AMD overnight, but is a big win because EPYC lands in a non-AMD accelerator system and validates AMD's confidential computing at a major hyperscaler.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Treat as a qualitative credibility win for AMD's confidential computing, not a near-term revenue mover.
insights.quote: For AMD, this is probably not going to drive a 10% server CPU market share gain overnight.
